headline: The lower easy-run HR has now survived the volume build, confirming the efficiency gain that was on trial.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The confirming test flagged last week has resolved in your favour. Easy-run heart rate has held down through the same weeks that saw the four-week block climb well above the prior one — the efficiency gain isn't an artefact of a light recovery stretch, it's persisting under real load. That's the signal worth taking away today.

Today's short, low-HR run fits the pattern rather than adding anything new: it's a light day sitting comfortably within a block that has otherwise pushed both volume and strength frequency. The strain:tolerance balance is sitting neutral, so you're absorbing this load rather than digging into it — appropriate roughly three weeks out from a self-supported coast-to-coast where durability, not peak sharpness, is the currency.

Last night's short sleep is worth noting only as context; it doesn't change anything, and it comes off the back of a genuinely long night two days prior.
watch_items: Whether pack-carry running enters the schedule in time to adapt the 6-8kg load demand before the crossing.
Whether ascent per run starts trending toward sustained climbing rather than the rolling profiles logged so far.
Whether the run of shorter nights this week extends, given the volume being absorbed alongside it.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 195 km vs 120 km prior block (+63%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 144 bpm vs 153 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 10 vs 7 runs)
▲ Zone 2: 426 min vs 180-240 min/week target (237% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 4.8%
▬ Strain:tolerance ratio 1.00 (MAINTAINING) (strain 78, tolerance 78); sleep averaging 7h23m over the same period
